The lock

So nobody taps their way into your word.

A touchscreen going around a table gets tapped by accident. By the next player's thumb, or by the table itself when somebody sets it down. The padlock is there to stop that.

What the padlock does

It sits at the top of the screen, just left of the home icon. While it's shut, nothing else on the screen answers you. Holding the button won't bring the word up. The arrow won't move you on. Tap the padlock and everything works again.

Read this before somebody thinks it's broken

A locked screen looks exactly like a frozen one. It's not. Look at the top of the screen, tap the padlock, and carry on.

Off, Manual, Auto

The Lock tile in settings cycles through all three. It arrives switched off, so nothing locks until you decide you want it to. Turning it on from Off, or back off from Auto, asks you to confirm first, so a stray tap can't change it.

  • Off. No padlock at all, and nothing ever locks.
  • Manual. The padlock is there and you shut it and open it yourself.
  • Auto. The box locks itself the moment you tap Next and hand it on. The next player taps the padlock, sees their word, taps Next, and it locks again behind them. Nobody can thumb their way into somebody else's word on the way across.
It only locks while the cards go around

Once everyone has looked, it stops. The talk screen and the tag play screen are shared, and locking those would just be in the way. A fresh round never starts locked.
